item.title: Cooper's Way
item.description:
Architectural Principles & Engineering Directives Link to heading

Complex distributed systems, whether pricing equity derivatives or orchestrating asynchronous browser workers, tend to degrade when incidental complexity is introduced under the guise of cleverness. Over decades of designing and delivering platforms for global financial institutions, I have refined Cooper’s Way—a unified set of architectural directives, concurrency invariants, and coding standards designed to keep software deterministic, observable, and easy to maintain.

item.title: High-Performance Go Systems & Data Pipelines
item.description:
Zero-Allocation Stream Processing and Data Ingestion Link to heading

Processing multi-gigabyte personal data archives and high-volume email mailboxes presents significant memory management and resilience challenges. In-memory object deserialization quickly leads to GC pauses, memory exhaustion, and unrecoverable failures when batch jobs crash midway through execution. This project encompasses a suite of high-throughput CLI utilities, concurrent stream parsers, and data ingestion microservices engineered in Go to achieve deterministic memory bounds, sub-millisecond inter-process communication, and resume-safe state execution.

item.title: Enterprise Chromium Extension Ecosystem
item.description:
High-Throughput Concurrency in Manifest V3 Link to heading

Modern browser extensions operating under the Chromium Manifest V3 specification face strict architectural constraints: ephemeral service worker lifecycles, background execution quotas, and the constant risk of saturating the browser main thread during heavy data processing. This project is a monorepo ecosystem of five standalone Chromium extensions powered by a shared core kernel that provides deterministic task scheduling, dynamic worker pool auto-scaling, and persistent state recovery.
